result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` so they now follow their docstrings. All 150 rules now pass the check.

**How I checked:** I read each rule's docstring (type, %, threshold, cap) and wrote a separate reference version that follows the module docstring's common rules. I then compared all 150 rules against it over 160+ quantities and 18 unit prices. Before the fixes 11 rules disagreed; afterwards none did. The check script is in `/tmp/chk/check.py` and is not part of the repo.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | The cap was applied to the price before the discount was calculated, not to the discount | `disc = base*5//100` then `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 36 | The 50,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 100,000 | Always cap |
| 40 | `qty > 12`, so 12 units got no discount | `qty >= 12` |
| 42 | A marginal rule calculated on the whole amount | `(qty - 30) * unit * 12 // 100` |
| 63 | 9% applied, should be 8% | Changed to 8 |
| 70 | The 30,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 60,000 | Always cap |
| 85 | 6% applied, should be 5% | Changed to 5 |
| 113 | `qty > 100`, so 100 units got no discount | `qty >= 100` |
| 134 | 3% applied, should be 2% | Changed to 2 |
| 137 | `round()` rounded to the nearest won instead of rounding down | `// 100` |
| 140 | Same as 137 | `// 100` |

I also changed rule 82 from `qty >= 51` to `qty >= 50`. This doesn't change any result, because a marginal rule's discount is 0 at exactly 50 units anyway. I only did it so the code matches the docstring.

STATUS: DONE
